coverage.assessment: Three revision cuts leave later lines with less to rest on. Para 2 loses the 'interest' premise that V2 answers. Para 4 loses the 1838-onward framing behind 'all this that was being done.' Para 19 loses the setup for 'nor about Churches' (F1, F2, F6).

The revision improves referents ('the President brought up', 'Mr. Everett', 'Louisa Catherine'). Both the fall at Mount Vernon Street and the scene 'on the floor of the House' are kept, and the walk's staircase-to-school geography is intact.
The gardener's line survives verbatim and is correctly attributed. The President's wordless intervention, the chapter's key 'speech' by silence, is preserved.

'Probably' for Polk, 'could never make up his mind' on the fever, 'six...seven at the utmost' and 'close on eighty' all survive. The 1848 coda loses the boy's stated ignorance ('could under no circumstances have guessed') that frames the old man's knowledge counterfactual (F8).
The dual child/old-man perspective holds ('Then and always', 'Sixty years afterwards'). There is no premature revelation, and the star is correctly not mentioned.

Double hyphens and the periodic cadences are kept. However, the mock-legal irony after the walk was thinned in the first draft. The Madam's 'cross/charm' chiasmus is cut, and a cut leaves a grammatical residue ('every Adams, had lived') (F4, F5, F7).

The winter/summer opposition survives in its aphorisms. The revision, however, drops the explicit claim that it ran through life as 'irreducible opposites' to 'the last year of study,' weakening the chapter's link to the closing theory (F3).
All six local endpoints and their published partner endpoints are present. Partner 001, a preface, is omitted for dependency 1, but 031 carries the endpoint.

findings.claim: The revision cuts the closing sentence of para 2, which the first draft kept. That sentence makes the education interesting 'only with that understanding' of full partnership. V2's 'this is the only interest in the story' now answers a premise the reader no longer has. The 'consenting, contracting party' sentence survives, but it is no longer tied to why the story matters.
findings.counterevidence: The consent idea and 'excellent hand' survive, as the plan requires.

evidence.quote: Only with that understanding--as a consciously assenting member in full partnership with the society of his age--had his education an interest to himself or to others.
Only with that understanding--as a consciously assenting member in full partnership with the society of his age--had his education an interest to himself or to others.
To his life as a whole he was a consenting, contracting party and partner from the moment he was born to the moment he died.
but this is the only interest in the story, which otherwise has no moral and little incident.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the 'Only with that understanding...' sentence after 'the moment he died.'

findings.reader_effect: The argumentative hinge between the card-game consent and the authorial statement of method weakens. V2 reads as a free-standing quip rather than a qualification of the preceding claim.
findings.title: Para 2 loses the premise that the consenting partnership gives the education its 'interest'

Para 4 now opens abruptly with 'For him, alone.' V3's 'all this that was being done' then points only to May 1844 events, which the next sentences place after a memory from age three in 1841.
findings.counterevidence: 1838 remains prominent in paras 1–2, so dependency 0 is unaffected.

strengths: The school-walk sequence is intact: the mother's disadvantage as a guest, the silent descent, the boy's 'strategical points turned,' and the release only inside the school.
The revision fixes first-draft referents: 'which the President brought up,' 'How could Mr. Everett say,' and 'Louisa Catherine was born.'
Optional units are cut cleanly. The cottage and silver mugs go together, the Parkman/Degrand detail goes, and 'Indeed' is dropped once para 25 is gone.
All eight verbatim passages survive, including V3 and V8 at the chapter's turns.
Continuity checks hold: 'Probably' for Polk, the uncertainty about the fever, both the Mount Vernon Street fall and the House scene, and 'his uncle, Edward Everett.'
summary: The revision keeps all eight verbatim passages, every essential episode, and all six dependencies. The school walk is complete, and the optional cottage and silver-mug material is cut cleanly. It also fixes several first-draft referents: the President brings up the peaches, Mr. Everett is named in the eulogy questions, and Louisa Catherine is named before 'Louisa.' No blocker remains. Several small revision cuts remove connective premises: why the education has interest, the 1838–41 framing of 'all this,' the seasons running to the 'last year of study,' and the setup for 'nor about Churches.' The cuts also leave a stray-comma residue, and first-draft cuts had already thinned the mock-political irony after the walk.
